name: Sepharvaim
overview: Sepharvaim is identified in Scripture as an Assyrian city from which the king of Assyria relocated people to inhabit the cities of Samaria, replacing the Israelites (2 Kings 17:24). The inhabitants of Sepharvaim are noted for their idolatrous practices, including child sacrifice to their gods Adrammelech and Anammelech (2 Kings 17:31). The biblical narrative challenges the power of these gods, questioning their ability to deliver Samaria from judgment and captivity (2 Kings 18:34; Isaiah 36:19). Additionally, the text references the kings of Sepharvaim alongside other regional rulers, emphasizing the city's political and religious significance in the Assyrian empire (2 Kings 19:13; Isaiah 37:13).
